description: Gold-set for the deterministic composition logic around red-flag severity — everything downstream of the (model-assisted, not evaluated here) deterministic rule match and model propose step. §4.0.3: model may raise, never lower. §4.0.2: WARNING+ always carries a template, falling back to the generic escalation template. §4.0.7/§4.0.8: action-taken derivation and the sticky session floor never lower an in-turn severity. RED_FLAG_RULESET_VERSION bumps and any change to this composition logic should re-run this suite (npm run eval) before shipping — this is the layer c_urgent_needs_template and c_urgent_template_only (Annex A) actually depend on being correct.

clampSeverity_cases.description: Model proposes higher than the rule-matched base — raise applies
Model proposes lower than the rule-matched base — ignored, never lowers
No rule matched (NORMAL base), model proposes the maximum severity

resolveTemplateRequirement_cases.description: Below WARNING needs no template even if the rule happened to carry one
WARNING+ with a rule-supplied template uses that template
EMERGENCY with no rule-supplied template falls back to the generic escalation template
A model-driven raise past WARNING with a template-less rule still gets the generic fallback, not a null template_id

deriveActionTaken_cases.description: Emergency template shown wins regardless of the severity argument passed alongside it
EMERGENCY severity with the template shown is still TEMPLATE_SHOWN, not ESCALATED
WARNING with no template shown escalates
CRITICAL with no template shown escalates
MONITOR alone is logged but takes no action

applySessionFloor_cases.description: An active floor raises a lower in-turn severity
An active floor never lowers a higher in-turn severity
A cleared (inactive) floor is ignored entirely
No floor at all is a no-op
Equal floor and in-turn severity is a no-op (stays at that severity)
